About MITS
History
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior was established in 1957 by His Highness Sir Jiwaji Rao Scindia, Maharaja, of the erstwhile state of Gwalior under open door policy of Govt. of India. The foundation stone of the institute was laid by the then President Dr. Rajendra Prasad, on 28th October, 1956 and the building was inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan on 11th December, 1964. On the occasion of Golden Jubilee Celebrations of the institute, the president of India, Dr. Pratibha Devi Singh Patil graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of the institute as Chief Guest on 30th June, 2008. A postal stamp on MITS was also released on this occasion.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Autonomy & Accreditation
The institute is declared Deemed to be University under Distinct Category by Ministry of Education, Government of India in the year 2024. The institute is accredited by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) with A++ Grade (CGPA 3.53) for 5 years from 2023. Many of the programmes are accredited by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA).

Quality Culture
An Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) was established in December 2016 to evolve mechanism and procedures for measuring, monitoring and evaluating quality for various academic and administrative activities of the institution, for the internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

TEQIP Funding
The institute successfully completed the Technical Education Quality Improvement programme (TEQIP-Phase II) of MHRD and received ‘A’ grade in six of the seven performance criterions. Further, the institute is now on board TEQIP-III.

MOODLE Server
The institute started its own MOODLE Server (Modular Object-Oriented Dynamic Learning Environment) on 15th august 2017 for open source course management system to facilitate E-learning, Evaluation, Test / Quiz Conduction, Uploading Assignments etc.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Campus, Courses & Centres
The institute has a lush green environment conscious campus of around 44.6 acres which also includes ‘Madhav-Van’ a small teak wood forest where a large variety of birds can be sighted. The Institute offers 19 Bachelors, 11 Masters and Doctoral Degrees Programmes in Engineering and Technology. The Institute is a recognized Quality Improvement Programme (QIP) Centre for PG and Ph.D programs. The prime objective of the institute is to provide quality technical education at undergraduate and postgraduate levels.There is Study Centre of Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) and Nodal centre of RGPV, Bhopal.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Local Centre of NPTEL
NPTEL(National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning) Local Chapter has been established on 30th Oct 2017 to provide e-learning through on-line Web and Video courses in Engineering, Sciences, Technology among students.

Infrastructure
The Institute has state-of-the-art infrastructure encompassing spacious class rooms equipped with power point projectors, well equipped laboratories, three boys hostels, two girls hostels, Play ground, Gymnasium, Dispensary, Bank, ATM, Stationary & Photocopy shop, Canteen, Amul Parlour, Coffee Shop etc.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Central Library currently houses over 1,00,000 books, e-journals from Science Direct, ASME and ASCE under E-Shodh Sindhu & INFLIBNET consortium. The Institute has a high speed LAN with backbone of optical fiber and manageable switches. The institute is equipped with 1000 MBPS leased line from BSNL, which is providing high speed 24x7 internet facility in each nook and corner of the Institute.

Entrepreneurship Development Cell
The institute has DST established Entrepreneurship Development Cell, since 1988. The cell is active throughout the year and conducts various job oriented/innovative certificate courses, Faculty Development Programmes, Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps, Conferences and other activities.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Professional Society Chapters & Club Activities
To harness the immense potential and vivacious energy of the students for their all round personality development and confidence building, the institute provided a very active NSS and NCC wing, 07 Chapters of National/International Professional Societies (ISTE, IEEE, IET, ACM,CSI,IETE and SAE-INDIA) & 60 different institute level student clubs in wide areas ranging from technology, art, music, dance, meditation, yoga, health, sports, environment, social awareness etc.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > About Mits

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > About Mits]

Sports Facilities
The institute has cricket, basketball, football and tennis grounds, and badminton court along with facilities for indoor games. The institute has been successively receiving awards and top ranks in many sporting events such as Table-Tennis, Badminton, and Basket-ball at the nodal and state level. Prizes are also won in Kho-Kho, chess and football.

Duties and Responsibilities

Dean, Faculty of Engineering & Technology:
o The Dean Faculty of Engineering & Technology will be the academic head of the MITS-DU.
o The Dean FoET will have the right to approve & forward the papers/documents of faculty & staff related to academics /HR development etc. (excluding service-related documents).
o The Dean FoET will prepare the institutional development plan (lDP) for the future.
o The Dean FoET will overall monitor the accreditation of institution/programmes by different agencies and coordinate with the various committees.
o The Dean FoET is authorized to conduct / chair meetings of MITS-DU on behalf of the Vice Chancellor.
o The Dean FoET will issue necessary directions for implementation of the ordinances and other decisions.
o The Dean FoET will monitor the activities of various chapters including student chapters.
o The vision document of MITS-DU will be prepared by the Dean FoET in consultation with other important stakeholders.
o Review of the feedback/survey formats/questionnaires and update from time to time for internal/external stakeholders will be carried out by the Dean FoET.
o The Dean FoET will maintain the records of Doctoral and Post Doctoral students.
o The Dean FoET will be responsible for the conduct and maintenance of the standards of teaching, research and human resource of the MITS-DU and shall have such other functions as may be prescribed by the rules of the lnstitution Deemed to be University and assigned by Vice Chancellor/Pro Chancellor & Chancellor.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Duties And Responsibilities

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Duties And Responsibilities]

Dean (Quality Assurance):
o Will coordinate the MITS-DU's quality assurance system including strategic planning, assessment and evaluation for continuous improvement, statistical analysis of instrumentation to establish validity and reliability and data dissemination.
o Will act as Management Representative for ISO activities and will be responsible for restructuring / revising of the Quality Management System with a focus on NBA, NAAC, NIRF and other such requirements.
o Will look after the NBA, NAAC, Autonomy and ISO reports and other such documentation and preparations.
o Will ensure overall planning and implementation of quality assurance and quality enhancement activities within the MITS-DU.
o Will work for promotion, enhancement and dissemination of good teaching and learning practices and will monitor the regular class room teaching in Face to Face (FF)/blended mode.
o Will spearhead the activities of lnternal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) towards assertion of quality in consultation with Dean FoET.
o Supervise & maintain quality of food served in canteens & Hostel Mess.
o Other work assigned by Dean FoET/V|ce Chancellor.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Duties And Responsibilities

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Duties And Responsibilities]

Dean (Academics):
o To ensure adherence to the ordinances as approved by the Academic Council.
o To Conduct meetings and monitor academic activities in consultation with Dean FoET.
o To conduct the meetings of academic cells.
o To prepare the MITS-DU Academic Calendar.
o To advise examination body regarding the academic rules and practices.
o Plan expansion of academic programmes.
o To work for lnternationalization / National Collaborations in the field of academics.
o To supervise the registration of students through a duly constituted committee.
o To supervise the awards of Medals for Meritorious students.
o To create more Centers of Excellence (CoE) and monitor collaborative activities.
o To monitor the upkeep and upgradation of library and other learning resources.
o To chair the meetings pertaining to academics on behalf of the Dean FoET.
o To address other matters as may be referred by the Dean FoET.
o He/She will report to Dean Faculty of Engineering & Technology.
o Any other work assigned by Dean FoET/Vice Chancellor.

Dean (Research):
o To advise and device policies for various Faculty and Staff Development programmes for qualification upgradation in consultation with Dean FoET.
o To enhance lndustry MITS-DU linkages, collaborative research, entrepreneurship and incubation centers.
o To motivate faculty to write and apply for sponsored research projects.
o To monitor the effective utilization of funds of externally funding projects.
o To maintain and update records of research publications.
o To ensure sponsoring faculty members for attending Conferences/Seminars/ Workshops as per MITS-DU norms.
o To chair the meetings pertaining to research on behalf of the Dean FoET.
o He/She will report to Dean Faculty of Engineering & Technology.
o Any other work assigned by Dean FoET/Vlce Chaneelior.

Dean (Public Relations):
o To liaison between parents, outside world and MITS-DU administration.
o To look after the dissemination of information to outside world including print media, social media and other agencies.
o To supervise the admission process of students at lnstitutional level through duly constituted committees.
o To Coordinate Community Development programmes and social development activities.
o Act as University-lndustry interface including publicity, news bulletins, brochures preparation/distribution, etc.
o To obtain and analyse feedback from students, other internal stakeholders, industries / parents and conduct exit survey for outgoing batch and alumni tracer studies for passed out batches.
o He/She will report to Dean Faculty of Engineering & Technology/Vice Chancellor.

[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Duties And Responsibilities]

Dean (Student Administration):
o To head the discipline committee of the MITS-DU.
o To maintain campus discipline of the students and coordinate the same with the Chief Warden in the smooth functioning of the hostels.
o To work as Chairperson of the Proctorial Committee to prevent ragging.
o To encourage healthy living and lively positive relationships among students and the campus community.
o To analyse placement data to gather an understanding for future trends and articulate needs for university level planning.
o Regularly meet with faculty members to solicit the expertise in placement activities with regard to initializing and planning for future activities.
o To interact with students to keep them informed about the latest market trends and skills & demands so that they can update themselves and prepare best for their career.
o To boost up student morale and counsel them before they undergo summer and final placement activities.
o To provide feedback to faculty members on placement opportunities.
o To build relationships with alumni through seminars, annual meets, etc.
o To plan for accommodation of parents and family members of students during Admission, Convocation, etc.
o To interact with the medical and psychological staff.
o To draft policies, rules & regulations for the functioning of the students.
o To take proper steps in respect of the grievances of students regarding the facilities available to them in the libraries, hostel common rooms and health centres.
o He/She will report to Vice Chancellor.
o Any other work assigned by the Vice Chancellor.

Dean (Student Welfare):
o To promote extra-curricular activities such as games, sports, N.C.C. etc.
o To coordinate between students and administration for extracurricular and co-curricular and Plan and organize various co- and extra-curricular activities.
o To work on the annual budget allocated for the Students Affairs and activities through Clubs/ Societies including Sports and Tech fests and manage spending in a manner that develops policies regarding student Iife.
o Manage, and act as Faculty Advisor for Students events.
o To liaison between university administrators and student organizations, such as student clubs and societies etc. on campus.
o Monitor day-to-day essential support required for co-curricular activities of students.
o Arrange for special care for the weaker and needy sections of students.
o Prepare plan and execute programmes for holistic development of the students.
o Nominate student representatives to various bodies of the University in consultation with Dean, Student Administration.
o Co-ordinate with the office of the Chief Warden in the smooth functioning of the hostels.
o Enable and facilitate conduct of sports and cultural events on the campus.
o Co-ordinate with the sports and cultural in-charges and committees etc. for all matters to students' welfare.
o Students to participate events/programmes outside the University in consultation with Dean, Student Administration.
o Keep in touch with the guardians as and when required.
o Co-ordinate with the Dean, Student Administration on matters related to students' discipline in the University.
o To promote and encourage cultural, social and literary activities with a view to fostering health, corporate life in the student community.
o To establish and direct programmes for guidance and counselling of students.
o He/She will report to Dean Student Administration/Vice Chancellor.
o Any other work assigned by Dean, Student Administration/Vice Chancellor.

Registrar:
o Will be ln-charge of Student Section of the MITS-DU.
o To monitor the admissions of all courses in the MITS-DU.

General Service Rules/Conditions
a. Short Titles and Commencement:-
These rules shall be called "The Madhav Institute of Technology &Science (Deemed University), Gwalior, Service (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) rules"
These rules will be in force from the date of approval by the Chancellor on the recommendation of Executive Council of the MITS-DU for those employees who are in service and for those who will join the MITS-DU in future.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

b. Definitions:-
In these rules:
'Society' means the "The Scindia Engineering College Society Gwalior".
'President' means the President of Board of Governors of the Society.
'Board' means the Board of Governors of Society.
'Executive Council' means the Executive Council as per UGC (deemed to be university) regulations 2023
'Finance Committee' means the Finance Committee as per UGC (deemed to be university) regulations 2023.
'Selection Committee' means the Faculty/Staff Selection Committee appointed by the Chancellor/Vice Chancellor for the selection of faculty/staff of the Institute.
The Vice Chancellor, will be appointed by President, The Scindia Engineering College Society Gwalior.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

c. Cadre:-
The strength of the Services (Human Resource requirement) and the Scales shall be determined by the Executive Council from time to time. The Chancellor on the recommendation of Executive Council may increase or decrease the strength by creation/reduction of additional, permanent, or temporary posts, as may be found necessary from time to time as per academic and administrative requirements.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

d. Classification of Posts:
The posts under the employment of the MITS-DU shall be classified as follows:-
(A) Class I Posts: (i.)Professor, (ii) Associate Professor, (iii) Assistant Professor, (iv) System Analyst
(B) Class II Posts :(i) Training & Placement Officer,(ii) Librarian, (iii) Physical Training Instructor,(iv) Finance Officer (v) Accounts Officer, (vi) Student Counsellor, (vii) Programmer, (viii) Assistant Engineer, (ix) General Assistant Surgeon/Medical Officer, (x) Foreman
(C) Class III Posts: Technical &Non-Technical Staff
(D) Class IV Posts
Details of the posts shall be reviewed from time to time by the Executive Council of the MITS-DU. The above posts may be filled through regular, contractual and contingency appointments/engagements. The Chancellor on the recommendation of Executive Council may increase/decrease the above classification as per requirement and prevailing UGC norms.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

e. Scope and Application: -
These rules shall apply to every member in the regular/temporary services of "Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (Deemed University)" run by the "The Scindia Engineering College Society, Gwalior".

f. Recruitment:-
Recruitment for the teaching posts shall be made as per the norms & regulations issued by MoE/UGC from time to time. Recruitment of Regular Faculty/Staff shall be made by the faculty/Staff Selection Committee of the MITS-DU constituted as per MoE/UGC norms approved by Chancellor on the recommendation of Executive Council. Non-Teaching posts will be as per the approval of Chancellor on the recommendation of Executive Council from time to time and in force at the time of advertisement/recruitment.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

g. Conditions of Eligibility of Direct Recruitment: -
The candidate, must satisfy the conditions with regard to minimum/maximum age, educational qualifications and experience as specified from time to time by the Executive Council in accordance with the MoE/UGC norms as applicable in force from time to time. However, Executive Council has a right to increase the minimum Qualifications for the recruitment of Teaching & Non-Teaching Staff (Technical or Non Technical) to ensure the quality recruitments.

h. Appointment by Promotion:-
Selection and/ or Promotion of faculty (Teaching posts) shall be as per the latest MoE/UGC rules and regulation. Executive Council has a right to increase the minimum Qualifications/requirement for the promotion of Teaching & Non-Teaching Staff to ensure maintain the quality.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

i. Conditions of Eligibility for Promotion:-
i. The Selection Committee constituted as per MoE/UGC norms shall consider the cases of all eligible faculty for the Promotion of faculty (Teaching posts) who fulfill the minimum conditions with regard to experience, educational qualifications, research outcomes and other conditions according to MoE/UGC/ Executive Council.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

j. Appointing Authority:-
Appointment for the post of Vice Chancellor shall be made by the President of the Society.
Regular Appointments through open selection for the Class I & II posts shall be made by the Vice Chancellor on behalf of Executive Council on the recommendation of the Selection committee constituted in accordance with MoE/UGC norms and approval of Selection Committee Minutes by Chancellor.
Appointments to all other posts shall be made by the Vice Chancellor on the recommendations of the Staff Selection Committee of the MITS-DU approved by Executive Council.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

k. Probation
Every person recruited directly or promoted (to any cadre) on appointment in or against a substantive post shall be placed on probation for a period of three years which may be further extended on the basis of annual performance.
Services of any employee can be discontinued during the probation period if his/her performance is found unsatisfactory.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

Confirmation:-
A person appointed to a post on probation shall be confirmed to the post only on his/her satisfactory completion of probation and condition (if any) along-with his/her fitness for confirmation having been duly certified by the competent authority i.e the Vice Chancellor in all except his own.
Services of any employee can be discontinued by the appointing authority during probation period if he / she is found involved in acts of indiscipline, misconduct, corruption, malpractices or misuse of his /her position.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

m. Seniority:-
The seniority of faculty members will be determined in the following manners:-
Without prejudice to the existing inter seniority of the teaching staff, the seniority among future recruits shall ordinarily be fixed with reference to the date of their joining the post. if, however, more than one person joins on the same date the seniority will be determined by the priority fixed by the selection committee based on merit.
The seniority of the candidates taken by the promotion vis-à-vis the direct recruits shall be fixed with reference to the length of service, experience and record of the promotees, Subject to this general working rule, the seniority shall ordinarily be governed by the date of promotion to the post.
Seniority among the candidates taken up by promotion to a particular grade will be according to the date of promotion to that grade.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

n. Pay/Salary:-
The salary (scales of pay, dearness allowance and other components) admissible to the faculty & staff shall be as per the approval of Vice Chancellor, on the recommendation of Executive Council in accordance with MoE/UGC scales as applicable time to time.

o. Increments:-
As per the scale applicable to the cadre, further MoE/UGC rules may be referred.
The sanction to draw increments shall be given by the competent authority after evaluation/review of performance appraisal/API as per MITS-DU norms in accordance with MoE/UGC norms as applicable.
Each order withholding an increment shall state the period for which it is withheld and also whether the postponement shall have the effect of postponing future increments.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

p. Rules Regarding Leave, Provident Fund & Medical Attendancе And Journey On Duty:-
All employees of the MITS-DU shall have the benefit of Employee Provident fund and shall be subject to Employee Provident Fund and M.P. Act 1952-7A trust Rules and amendments as applicable.
Leave rules will be as per M.P. Civil Service (Leave) Rules 1977 and amendments as applicable for the employees of this MITS-DU.

Retirement from Service:-
Retirement age of faculty & Staff shall be as per the decision of Executive Council from time to time.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

r. Termination of Services:-
The appointing authority may terminate the services of any regular member of the staff after giving him/her three months notice or three months pay in lieu thereof, on negligence of duties or not fulfilling qualification of the position/post, on medical ground's or on account of inefficiency, or for any similar grounds or his retention in service is considered undesirable.
A permanent member of the staff may at any time, resign his/her post after giving three months notice in writing to the appointing authority or three months pay in lieu thereof.
The services of the regular staff during the period of probation or temporary/contractual staff shall be terminated by the competent authority after giving one, month's notice in writing or one month's pay in lieu of notice subjected to completion of Academic Semester in progress or as per decision of competent authority (in case of temporary/contract staff).
Members of the staff on probation may give one month's notice of resignation or pay an amount equal to one month's salary together with all allowances in lieu thereof.
The appointing authority is empowered to dismiss any member of the staff from service, without any notice or compensation on grounds of misconduct, which is considered so grave as to render his/her continuance in service seriously detrimental to the interest of the MITS-DU after proper enquiry. In case of Pending enquiry, the appointing authority may suspend forthwith. The person who has been dismissed shall have the right to appeal to the Executive Council whose decision shall be final. If the appeal is upheld by the Executive Council, the person shall, be reinstated in-service, on such terms as the Executive Council may decide. During the period of suspension, a subsistence allowance amounting half the basic pay shall be paid and dearness allowance regulated accordingly.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Service Rules]

s. Punishments and Appeals:-
(A) The following penalties may, for good and sufficient reasons, be imposed on An MITS-DU employee, i.e.
i. Warning
ii. Fine
iii. Withholding increments with or without giving any reason
iv. Reduction of pay (i.e.) to a lower state in time scale if the post carried a timescale.
v. Reduction in rank/cadre (Demotion)
vi. Suspension
vii. Compulsory Retirement
viii. Removal from service
ix. Dismissal from Service
x. Recovery against pecuniary loss caused to the MITS-DU due to negligence of breach of orders.
(B) Before imposing penalties prescribed above, on a MITS-DU employee, he / she shall be called upon to explain in writing, his/her conduct or an enquiry shall be initiated by an official or committee constituted for the purpose, giving the employee adequate opportunity of defending himself/herself. Such explanation or papers of enquiry shall be part of the record. No penalty shall be imposed under clauses (iv), (v), (vii), (viii) & (ix) on a person appointed by the MITS-DU and this again shall be subject to ratification by the Executive Council at the next meeting.
(C) Every person shall be entitled to appeal to the next higher authority from an order imposing on him/her any of the penalties. The Executive Council decision shall be final, in case of person appointed by the MITS-DU, although no right of appeal from an order passed by the MITS-DU subsists yet it shall be open to the person concerned to file review application to the Executive Council.
(D) Appeals under (c) above shall be preferred within three months from time date on which the applicant was informed of the orders appealed against. They should contain all material statements and a cogent statement or the arguments, relied on by the appellant, and be free from disrespectful or acrimonious Language.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Service Rules

content:

t. Interpretation:-
If any question arises relation to the inter predation of these rules it shall be referred to the Executive Council whose decision shall be final and binding on the parties concerned.

u. Relaxation:-
Nothing in these rules shall be construed to limit or abridge the powers of the MITS-DU to deal with the case of any person to whom these rules apply in such manner as may appear to it (MITS-DU) to be just and equitable; provided that the case shall not be dealt with in any manner less favorable to him/her than that provided in these Rules.

w. Delegation of Powers:-
These powers are subjected to change from time to time as per the need and requirement of the MITS-DU.

Employee and the Employer, both the parties shall always legally bind with the terms & conditions.

[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message]

Vice Chancellor's Message

Vice Chancellor
Dr. Rajindra Kumar Pandit

From the Vice Chancellor’s Desk………
Dear Students, Parents, Alumni, and Corporate Partners,

It brings me immense joy to share that Madhav Institute of Technology and Science (MITS), Gwalior, has successfully completed two years as a Deemed-to-be-University. In March 2024, the Ministry of Education, Government of India, on the advice of the UGC, granted us this prestigious status. Since our inception in 1957, MITS has proudly served the nation. Today, this milestone allows us to leverage academic autonomy to scale new heights of excellence for all our stakeholders.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message]

To Our Students and Parents: A Holistic Ecosystem
We are committed to nurturing well-rounded individuals through a dynamic curriculum that implements the National Education Policy (NEP-2020) in letter and spirit. We offer undergraduate programs across 19 disciplines, alongside cutting-edge B.Tech and newly launched Post-Graduate programs in emerging areas like Artificial Intelligence, Embedded Systems & VLSI, and the Internet of Things (IoT).
Our unique continuous evaluation model, relative grading, summer semesters, and credit transfers from MOOCs (NPTEL) encourage self-learning. Furthermore, our mandatory courses in Python, Data Science, and Machine Learning—paired with minor degree options—ensure that every student, regardless of their core branch, can thrive in an interdisciplinary world. Beyond academics, our vibrant, green campus and active student clubs ensure personal growth, leadership development, and options to develop excellent communication skills.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message]

To Our Corporate Partners: Industry-Ready Professionals
MITS is dedicated to producing engineers who can solve real-world challenges from day one. Our student-centric roadmap includes a dedicated credit course on Professional Skills and Competencies in the pre-final year. This is capped by a mandatory, full-time final-semester internship that provides students with practical corporate exposure before graduation.
Our students learn by doing. Equipped with state-of-the-art labs in Robotics, ML, AR/VR, and IoT, they actively transition from learners to innovators. This is proven by their consistent victories at premier global hackathons and their ability to build in-house digital portals that streamline our university operations, saving significant revenue and man-hours.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message]

To Our Global Alumni Network: A Legacy of Excellence
Our alumni are our greatest pride. You occupy highly placed, influential positions across global corporates, public sectors, railways, armed forces, administrative services, and academia. As MITS transitions into this distinct university era, your legacy remains our anchor. We are expanding our Ph.D. programs in thrust areas and funding high-productivity research to ensure your alma mater remains a globally recognized hub of innovation.

metadata.breadcrumbs: About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | About Institute > Vice Chancellor Message]

Looking Ahead
The Deemed-to-be-University status has allowed us to elevate our quality initiatives, fulfilling the national mandate of providing a holistic technical education that strengthens India's global footprint. On behalf of the management, faculty, and staff, I welcome our current and prospective students, and I wish you all the very best in your present and future endeavours.

The School of Applied Mathematics is dedicated to providing a strong foundation in mathematical sciences and their practical applications across engineering, technology, science, and interdisciplinary domains. With a focus on analytical thinking, mathematical modeling, and problem-solving, the School prepares students to address complex real-world challenges.

Through a blend of academic excellence and research-driven learning, the School of Applied Mathematics plays a vital role in supporting the academic and research activities of the Institute while equipping students with the quantitative skills required for higher studies, research, and professional careers.

Department: Department of Architecture & Planning
Laboratories

1. CAAD Lab
Students can improve their digital design skills by using the CAAD lab. The computers are equipped with the most recent design software and the student-to-machine ratio is kept at an optimal level. An internet connection, a printer, and a scanner are additional amenities at the Resource Centre. The following programmes are available: AutoCAD, Revit, Photoshop, 3ds Max, and SketchUp.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Architecture And Planning Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Architecture And Planning Department > Laboratory]

2. Climatology Lab
The Institute offers a well-equipped Climatology Lab to introduce the ideas of climatology, environmental studies, and landscape, which is a crucial component of architecture. The laboratory is equipped for measuring parameters of a building such as air temperature (dry bulb, wet bulb, globe, and WBGT) (both outdoor and indoor), Surface Temperature (IR based and K-type), Relative Humidity, Heat Index, Rainfall (weather station with outdoor and indoor unit), Wind velocity, flow & direction (anemometers & wind vane in weather station), etc.

3. GIS Lab
Students can improve their digital design skills by using the GIS lab. The computers are equipped with the most recent design software and the student-to-machine ratio is kept at an optimal level.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Architecture And Planning Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Architecture And Planning Department > Laboratory]

4. Material Lab
For students to refer to and practically comprehend real-world methods, many sorts of materials and product examples from industries are kept in the department. Samples are continually being added to this facility to improve it. UPVC window systems, paints and finishes, and construction blocks made of different materials are just a few of the samples available.
View More Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/electrical_engineering/Lab%20Manuals/MI%20Lab.pdf

5. Construction Yard
The students can experiment with different building materials and get a close-up look at how buildings are constructed thanks to the construction yard. They gain additional insight into the subject matter being covered in class through hands-on practical experience.

Department: Centre for Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Department)
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

Department Vision
To become a distinguished centre in Artificial Intelligence, empowering innovation, research and creating solutions to address real-world challenges with societal relevance.

Department Mission
- Deliver a cutting-edge curriculum in AI, AIML, AIDS, and AIR, empowering students with the skills to solve real-world challenges and lead in global technology.
- Promote a culture of research and innovation in AI, enabling impactful collaborations with industry and academia for technological advancement.
- Equip students to apply AI responsibly, ensuring ethical, societal, and human-centered solutions are at the core of their innovations.

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > About Ai Department]

About Artificial Intelligence Department / Centre for Artificial Intelligence
The Centre for Artificial Intelligence was Established in the year 2023. The objective is to nurture academic excellence, industry exposure and outstanding career opportunities to our students. The department consists of highly qualified faculty with doctoral degrees from reputed institutes of India and abroad. The department aims to train students as leaders in AI, DS & Robotics with world-class infrastructure, curriculum, and comprehensive hands-on experience through industry connect programs. The goal of the centre is to ensure academic excellence in students with wide exposure of research and career opportunities.

Department: Centre for Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Department)
Laboratories

1. Robotics Lab
The Robotics Laboratory is a state-of-the-art facility established to promote innovation, research, and hands-on learning in robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and intelligent machines. The laboratory is equipped with advanced infrastructure, including 3D Printers, Robotic Arms, High-Performance Computing (HPC) Systems, NVIDIA Jetson Nano Development Boards, and Aurion Robotics Kits, enabling students and researchers to design, prototype, and deploy robotic solutions.
The laboratory provides comprehensive facilities for the design, development, testing, and deployment of both humanoid and non-humanoid robots, catering to applications in automation, healthcare, manufacturing, agriculture, and smart environments. It also supports the development of Drones and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for aerial surveillance, mapping, monitoring, and autonomous navigation applications.
Students utilize the laboratory for academic projects, research activities, product prototyping, and participation in national and international competitions. The lab has a strong track record of excellence, with student teams winning numerous hackathons, robotics competitions, and innovation challenges, demonstrating their technical competence and innovative capabilities.
The Robotics Laboratory serves as a multidisciplinary innovation hub, fostering collaboration among students, faculty members, industry experts, and startups while encouraging the development of next-generation intelligent robotic systems and autonomous technologies.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory]

2. Programming Lab 1
Programming Lab 1 provides a computing platform for novel languages like Python and R for building a coherent set of ideas, fundamentals of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Deep Learning models and algorithms, and it facilitates students to practice basic programming in C, C++, and JAVA also. Each lab session is aimed to translate the theory lectures into practical implementation through programming paradigms and tools, and platforms provided in the data science lab.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory]

3. Programming Lab 2
Programming Lab 2 welcomes students, researchers, interns, faculties, newbies, and everyone from a broad range of disciplines who are fascinated with the possibilities of turning big and complex data into knowledge. Members of the data science lab seek cutting-edge problem-based solutions to data mining, computer vision, and machine learning problems arising in numerous application areas involving data analytics.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory]

4. High Performance Computing (HPC) Lab
HPC Lab is equipped with a wide range of powerful computers with high-end graphics cards that are essential for research. The HPC Lab brings together researchers interested in developing fast, reliable, and robust numerical algorithms needed for modeling and simulation in a variety of fields including database management, Numerical linear algebra, Optimization, etc. The requirement of modern days is to have an automated system that manages, modifies, and updates data accurately. The lab aims at practicing and achieving this aim by using various software. All these require “hands-on” training in programming through practical projects.
Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Centre%20of%20Artificial%20Intelligence/Laboratories/HPC%20labaratory%20details.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Artificial Intelligence Department > Laboratory]

5. Augmented Reality & Virtual Reality Lab
The Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) Laboratory is an advanced interdisciplinary research and innovation facility dedicated to immersive technologies, human-computer interaction, and intelligent systems. The laboratory is equipped with cutting-edge infrastructure, including Meta Quest Headsets, Microsoft HoloLens Devices, Brain Signal Mapping Systems, High-Performance Computing (HPC) Systems, and Unity Development Software, enabling students and researchers to develop next-generation AR, VR, Mixed Reality (MR), and Extended Reality (XR) applications.
The laboratory provides a comprehensive environment for the design, development, and deployment of immersive digital experiences across diverse domains such as education, healthcare, industrial training, smart manufacturing, entertainment, and simulation. Students actively engage in AR/VR application development, 3D environment design, digital twin creation, immersive visualization, and interactive user experience development using industry-standard tools and platforms.
A unique research focus of the laboratory is the integration of Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technologies, where students and researchers work on projects involving brain signal acquisition, mapping, and interpretation for controlling robotic systems and intelligent devices through neural signals. This facilitates research in assistive technologies, neuro-robotics, and human-machine interaction.
The laboratory has contributed significantly to research and innovation, resulting in the publication of numerous research papers in reputed national and international journals and conferences. Student teams associated with the laboratory have consistently demonstrated excellence by securing top positions in various national-level hackathons, innovation challenges, and technology competitions across India.
The AR/VR Laboratory serves as a center of excellence for immersive technologies, fostering innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, research-driven learning, and the development of future-ready solutions at the intersection of virtual reality, artificial intelligence, robotics, and neuroscience.

About the Department:
The Chemical Engineering Department was started in 1996 and offers B.Tech/B.E. and M.Tech courses in Chemical Engineering. The department was started with 30 students in undergraduate studies, but later, recognizing the importance and growing industry demand for Chemical Engineers, the intake capacity was raised to 60 in 2013-14. The M.Tech course was started in 2013-14 with specialization in Chemical Engineering. The department was founded with the vision of developing into an academic center of excellence in Chemical Engineering and associated areas, preparing competitive professionals and experts equipped with knowledge, skills, and ethical attitude to serve the society and nation.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Civil Department > About Civil Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Civil Department > About Civil Department]

Civil Engineering is an NBA-accredited program
Department of Civil engineering is one of the pioneer department of the Institute, which commenced with the Inception of the Institute. At present department is offering B.Tech degree in Civil Engineering (4 year) and two post graduate courses i.e. M.E (Construction Technology & Management) and M.Tech (Structural Design) and Ph.D. Department has a quality improvement center for QIP programme which is under mentorship of IIT's. Department is well equipped with state of art instruments procured using various funding agencies including TEQIP II & III, AICTE grant and funds from various other agencies. To provide industrial exposure, the department is having MOU with CRRI (New Delhi), CBRI, NHAI & Gwalior smart city corporation limited. Department organizes regular field industrial visit to UG & PG students to provide them industrial exposure. Department regularly organizes seminars, workshops, STTP, expert lecture for knowledge and upgradation of skill of the students. For value addition of the students, department regularly conducts finishing school, remedial measures, novel engaging courses etc. Students are actively involved in Indian Concrete Institute (ICI) and Indian water works association (IWWA) activities. Department is leading resource center for providing consultancy services to various organizations. Leading academician, industrialist and students are involved in updating syllabus of the subjects through Board of studies and make course material relevant to present day requirement. Department is actively involved in research and development work for the benefits of students and society. Course curriculum of the B.Tech program is framed and designed as per National Education Policy, 2020.

Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO I The graduate of the program will have successful career in various domains of civil engineering.
PEO II The graduate of the program will be able to practice civil engineering in infrastructure industries, public sector undertakings and as an entrepreneur.
PEO III The graduate of the program will be able to pursue higher education for knowledge enhancement.
PEO IV The graduate of the program will be able to exhibit leadership skills, team spirit and ethical practices.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Civil Department > Pos Peos Psos

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Civil Department > Pos Peos Psos]

Program Outcomes (POs)
PO I Engineering Knowledge: The graduate will be able to apply knowledge of mathematics, science & design principles to solve the problems in civil engineering.
PO II Problem Analysis: The graduate will be able to identify, formulate and analyse engineering problems with substantial conclusions using analytical tools appropriate to civil engineering.
PO III Design/Development of Solutions: The graduate will be able to design civil engineering systems within realistic constraints to meet desired needs of economy, environment, society, health and safety.
PO IV Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: The graduate will be able to conduct investigations of complex problems by use of research based knowledge & methods including experimentation, interpretation of data & synthesis of information to provide valid conclusion.
PO V Modern Tool Usage: The graduate will be able to use the technical skills and modern engineering / computational tools for broadly defining engineering activities.
PO VI The Engineer and Society: The graduate will be able to assess safety & legal issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional civil engineering practice.
PO VII Environment and Sustainability: The graduate will be able to understand the impact of the professional civil engineering solutions in relation to societal needs, environmental concern & sustainable development.
PO VIII Ethics: The graduate will be able to understand the importance of professional ethics and norms of civil engineering practice.
PO IX Individual and Team work: The graduate will be able to function effectively as a member or leader in diverse teams
PO X Communication: The graduate will be able to communicate effectively with engineering community and society at large by being able to comprehend and write effective reports, prepare documentation and make effective presentation.
PO XI Project management and Finance: The graduate will be able to demonstrate knowledge of management and financial principles to civil engineering projects.
PO XII Life-long Learning: The graduate will be able to engage in lifelong learning & adapt to rapid changes in civil engineering and its allied areas.

PSO II The graduate will be able to understand the importance of uncertainty & risk involved in infrastructure projects and subsequently propose the solutions.

Computer Science and Design Department — MITS Gwalior
========================================================

About the Department
--------------------

The department of CSD has an excellent & rich history and an outstanding record of contributions to the profession and community. The department is well recognized for excellence in facilities and teaching.

The Department offers B.Tech. degrees. The Department has a comprehensive curriculum on topics related to all aspects of Computer Hardware and Software Design with an emphasis on practical learning. The course structure is up-to-date and includes courses on emerging topics to equip our students with the latest developments in Computer Science and Design.

================================================================

1. Computing Lab
   - Description: Computing lab is designed to develop basic to advance level computer skills in students coming from any field of study. It aims to provide students with an understanding of the role computation can play in solving problems of their field of study.
   - Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Computing%20LAB.pdf

   - Description: Data Science being the hottest job skill requirement. This Lab focuses on transforming data into valuable insight and applying machine learning and data mining to real-world problems in society and industry.
   - Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Data%20Science%20Lab.pdf

   - Description: Project Lab is used for conducting presentations and demonstrations related to Minor Projects, Major Projects, Internships, and other research activities.

   - Description: Programming Lab focuses on providing basic principles of C, C++, Java, and Python programming languages along with practical exposures like designing flowcharts, algorithms, debugging programs, etc.
   - Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Programming%20Lab.pdf

   - Description: Hardware Lab focuses on providing knowledge of computer hardware processors, motherboards, memories, different add-on cards, and other peripherals like printers, plotters, and scanners. Students are trained for the assembly and disassembly of PCs.

The lab is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of ML algorithms, data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation.

Department Mission
- To provide global benchmark education through Outcome-Based Education (OBE), nurturing strong computing, analytical, and problem-solving skills for developing future-ready professionals.
- To provide industry-oriented learning through innovative teaching practices and modern laboratories, enabling learners to develop global competencies in emerging technologies.
- To foster research, innovation, and entrepreneurship leading to Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), quality publications, interdisciplinary collaborations, and technological advancements.
- To develop innovative and ethically responsible engineers by providing a dynamic learning environment that emphasizes sustainability, lifelong learning, leadership, and excellence in emerging technological domains.

Department: Centre for Computer Science and Technology (CCST)
Laboratories

1. Computing and Design Lab (CoDe Lab)
The Computing and Design Lab is dedicated to developing problem-solving, analytical thinking, and design-oriented computing skills. The laboratory provides students with hands-on experience in algorithm development, computational modeling, data visualization, UI/UX prototyping, computer graphics, web technologies, and emerging design tools. It serves as a platform for interdisciplinary projects, innovation, and research, enabling students to transform creative ideas into practical digital solutions. The lab also supports learning in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, and Human-Computer Interaction through project-based activities and modern software tools.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory]

Key Objectives:
- Develop computational thinking and problem-solving abilities.
- Design and prototype software applications and digital interfaces.
- Apply algorithms and computational models to real-world problems.
- Foster innovation through project-based learning and interdisciplinary collaboration.
- Support research in emerging computing technologies.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory]

2. Programming Lab
The Programming Lab provides a strong foundation in programming concepts, software development, and coding practices. The laboratory enables students to gain practical experience in programming languages such as C, C++, Python, and modern development frameworks. It emphasizes structured programming, object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithms, database connectivity, web programming, and software engineering practices. The lab prepares students to design, develop, test, and deploy efficient software solutions while promoting logical reasoning, debugging skills, teamwork, and industry-oriented coding standards.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science And Technology Department > Laboratory]

Key Objectives:
- Build strong programming and software development skills.
- Strengthen understanding of data structures and algorithms through implementation.
- Develop debugging, testing, and code optimization skills.
- Familiarize students with integrated development environments (IDEs), version control, and collaborative software development.
- Prepare students for industry requirements, competitive programming, internships, and research projects.

Department Vision
To create professionally competent and socially responsible technocrats with latest knowledge and innovative ideas to uplift the academia, industry and society.

Department Mission
To achieve academic excellence by imparting in-depth knowledge to the students through effective pedagogies and practical exposure on latest tools and technologies.
To provide environment & opportunity for students to bring out their inherent talents for their overall development through training programs, workshops, projects and internships.
To promote innovative research in Computer Science and Engineering and interdisciplinary domains to cater the needs of the Government, Industry and Society.
To Educate and nurture entrepreneurial and ethical values through guidance and support.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > About Computer Science Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > About Computer Science Department]

Computer Science & Engineering program is NBA-accredited till 2028
The department of CSE has an excellent & rich history and an outstanding record of contributions to the profession and community. The department is well recognized for excellence in facilities and teaching. The Department offers B.Tech., M.Tech. and Ph.D degrees. The Department has a comprehensive curriculum on topics related to all aspects of Computer Hardware and Software with an emphasis on practical learning. The course structure is up-to-date and includes courses on emerging topics to equip our students with the latest developments in Computer Science and Engineering. The Department has state-of-the-art infrastructure and computing equipment supported by high speed Ethernet and wireless networks. Our faculty members aim at delivering top class education blending their rich research experience with classroom teaching. The Department has started a new ACM Chapter and signed an MoU with Infosys under Infosys Campus Connect Program.

[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory]

Laboratories - Department of Computer Science & Engineering

Computing Lab
Computing lab is designed to develop basic to advance level computer skills in students coming from any field of study. It aims to provide students with an understanding of the role computation can play in solving problems of their field of study.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Computing%20LAB.pdf

Data Science Lab
Data Science being the hottest job skill requirement. This Lab focuses on transforming data into valuable insight and applying machine learning and data mining to real-world problems in society and industry.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Data%20Science%20Lab.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory]

Project & Research Lab 1
Project Lab is used for conducting presentations and demonstration related to the Minor Projects, Major Projects, Internship and other activities.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Project%20Lab.pdf

Programming Lab
Programming Lab focuses on providing basic principles of C, C++, Java and Python programming languages along with the practical exposures like designing flowcharts, algorithms, how to debug programs etc.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Programming%20Lab.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory]

Hardware Lab
Hardware Lab Focuses on providing the knowledge of computer hardware processors, motherboards, memories, different add-on cards, and other peripherals like printers, plotters, and scanners. The students are trained for the assembly and disassembly of PCs.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/Computer-Science/Lab%20Images/Hardware%20Lab.pdf

Machine Learning Lab
The Machine Learning Lab is dedicated to providing students with in-depth knowledge and practical experience in the field of machine learning (ML). The lab is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of ML algorithms, data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory]

Cloud Computing Lab
The Cloud Computing Lab is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of cloud technologies and how they can be leveraged to build scalable, flexible, and cost-effective solutions. The lab focuses on both the theoretical foundations and practical applications of cloud computing.

Project & Research Lab 2
The Project & Research Lab 2 serves as an innovation hub where students engage in independent and collaborative research projects, applying theoretical knowledge to real-world problems. The lab encourages hands-on experience in designing, developing, and evaluating projects across a variety of domains, fostering both creativity and technical expertise.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Computer Science Department > Laboratory]

Project & Research Lab 3
The Project & Research Lab 3 builds on the foundational skills developed in Project & Research Lab 1, offering students the opportunity to engage in more advanced, complex research projects and deeper exploration of specialized topics. This lab focuses on fostering critical thinking, advanced problem-solving, and professional-level project execution through interdisciplinary research and development.

Department Vision
To Prepare Professionally Competent Electrical Engineers for Global Industrial requirements and Social needs.

Department Mission
Impart state-of-the-art technical education at UG, PG and Ph.D. levels through good academic support & facilities. (Academic Development).
Keep pace with the latest technological developments in the domain. (R&D Activities).
Effective interactions with industries, academia and other stakeholders. (Industrial & Societal needs)
Provide training on soft skills, managerial skills and professional ethics for the overall development of students and society in an ethical manner. (Human Potential Development).

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electrical Department > About Electrical Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electrical Department > About Electrical Department]

Electrical Engineering is an NBA-accredited program
School of Electrical Engineering is one of the oldest departments established in 1957 with an intake of 40. Currently, the department is offering undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctorate programs in various disciplines of Electrical Engineering. Presently the total intake of the B.Tech. program is 120 and the M.E. in “Industrial Systems & Drives” program is with an intake of 25.
The thrust areas of the department are Power systems, Power Electronics, Control and Biomedical Instrumentation.
The school educates the students to take up challenging jobs in a wide range of industries and engage in research & development activities for the betterment of society. The syllabi of the courses are continuously updated and the laboratories are modernised to reflect the rapid changes in technology.
The school offers M.E and Ph.D programs to produce quality research. It has state-of-the-art laboratories to provide hands-on experiences and support research activities.
The courses offered by the school cater to learning needs from the basics to the advanced level. In addition, the school offers a variety of discipline electives to cover modern technologies.
[About Electrical Engineering](https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/electrical_engineering/PosterBrochure/Electrical%20Poster_001.jpg)

Laboratories

Basic Electrical & Electronics Engineering (BEEE) Lab
Undergraduate First Year Lab: Major experiments are related to verification of KCL, KVL, Superposition theorem; Determination of choke coil inductance and resistance; Determination of efficiency and regulation of single phase transformer, SC and OC test on single phase transformer; DC Machine overview, use of Multimeter; Determination of Diode characteristics; Verification of truth table.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/electrical_engineering/Lab%20Manuals/Basic%20Electrical%20%20Electronics%20Lab.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electrical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electrical Department > Laboratory]

Electrical Machines Lab
Undergraduate Lab: Major experiments are related to parallel operation of two single phase transformer, direct load test on single phase transformer; Determination of internal and external characteristics of DC shunt generator, speed control of DC motor; No load and blocked rotor test on 3-phase squirrel cage and slip ring induction motor; Determination of OC and SC characteristics of alternators; Determination of regulation and alternator using synchronous impedance method and zero power factor method; Determination of V-curves of synchronous motor; Determination of direct axis and quadrature axis reactance of alternator using slip test.
Lab Manual / Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/electrical_engineering/Lab%20Manuals/Lab%20Electrical%20Machines.pdf

Section: Department Mission

Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering — MITS Gwalior
=============================================================================

Department Vision
-----------------

To develop globally competent, industry-ready, and research-oriented Electronics and Telecommunication professionals equipped to address societal challenges and emerging technologies.

Department Mission
------------------

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > About Ete Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > About Ete Department]
Section: About the Department

- To build a strong foundation through a quality curriculum, skill-based training, and modern pedagogical practices.
- To inculcate global competence, technical excellence, strong ethical values, leadership and a commitment to lifelong learning.
- To nurture employability skills and entrepreneurship through industry-driven projects, industry internships, and interdisciplinary collaborations.
- To promote societal progress and sustainability through research and innovation.

About the Department
--------------------

The Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering was established in 2015. The faculty members are actively engaged in research in areas such as Ad Hoc Networking, Image Processing, Wireless Communication, Microwave Engineering, Nanoelectronics, VLSI Design, and Antenna Theory.

Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering
=========================================================================

1. Basic Electronics Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Designing of Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers, Oscillators; Characteristics analysis of Diodes, BJT, and MOSFET. Electronic circuit design and verification using advanced workstations that incorporate a multimeter, function generator, power supply, and CRO in a single platform.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory
metadata.section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

2. Project Lab
   - Description: The purpose of the Project Laboratory is to enable students to get familiar with hardware and software tools through hands-on mode. Used for conducting presentations and demonstrations related to Minor Projects, Major Projects, Skill-based projects, Internships, and other activities. Provides space for students to apply theoretical knowledge and develop innovative solutions. The lab is equipped with hardware facilities like an Antenna Testing facility, Spectrum Analyzer, Digital Storage Oscilloscope, PCB-prototyping machine, Function generator, PCB Soldering / De-soldering machine, etc. Ph.D. and M.Tech scholars carry out their research in this lab.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory
metadata.section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

3. Computer Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate and Postgraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Basic Mathematical experiments using MATLAB / Scilab; Simulation of various engineering problems in MATLAB/Scilab and other tools; Qualnet: Network Simulation using GNS; CST Studio: Antenna designing.

4. Communication Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Sampling and reconstruction, pulse amplitude and pulse width modulation (PAM/PWM), generation and detection of Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK), Phase Shift Keying (PSK), and Frequency Shift Keying (FSK) signals using MATLAB / Scilab software and trainer modules.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory
metadata.section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics And Telecommunication Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

5. Digital and Microprocessor Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Assembly language programming to generate standard waveforms using DAC and display waveforms on CRO with 8085; obtaining 2's complement of numbers; interfacing 8253 Timer and 8255 with 8086 in different modes.

6. Engineering Foundation Lab (Applied Physics Laboratory)
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. The Physics Laboratory is designed to provide students with practical exposure to the fundamental principles of applied physics through carefully structured experiments. Enables students to understand and verify important concepts related to solid-state physics, optics, modern physics, electrical measurements, and fiber optics by correlating theoretical knowledge with hands-on experimentation.

Department of Electronics Engineering — MITS Gwalior
======================================================

Department Vision
-----------------

To Prepare Globally Competent Electronics Engineers for Industrial Challenges and Societal needs.

Department Mission
------------------

- To provide quality education through need based curriculum and effective teaching learning process.
- To imbibe professional ethics, leadership and entrepreneur skills with a passion for lifelong learning.
- Strengthening of employability skills through multidisciplinary projects and internships.
- To inculcate the spirit of innovation and research to serve the needs of the society and industry.

Accreditation
-------------

Electronics Engineering program is NBA-accredited till 2028.

About the Department
--------------------

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > About Electronics Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > About Electronics Department]
Section: Brochures & Links

The Department of Electronics Engineering was established in 1987. The department offers a UG programme in Electronics Engineering with an intake of 120 students, a PG programme in M.Tech. Embedded System and VLSI with an intake of 18 students, and a Ph.D. programme. 

The faculty members are actively engaged in cutting-edge research in the areas of Ad-hoc Networking, Image Processing, Wireless Communication, Microwave Engineering, Nano-electronics, VLSI, and Antenna Theory. Faculty members have published numerous papers in reputed National and International Journals.

The alumni of the department have secured prestigious positions in the higher echelons of society and the global technical world. A substantial number of graduates pursue higher studies for their M.Tech, MBA, and Ph.D. from premier institutes in India and abroad.

Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering
======================================================

1. Basic Electronics Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Designing of Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers, Oscillators; Characteristics analysis of Diodes, BJT, and MOSFET. Electronic circuit design and verification using advanced workstations that incorporate a multimeter, function generator, power supply, and CRO in a single unified platform.
   - Details / Manual: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bCFQMXbQbfGEFFyRd4-sDlFocofSqWRL/view?usp=sharing

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

2. Project Lab
   - Description: The purpose of the Project Laboratory is to enable students to get familiar with hardware and software tools through hands-on mode. Used for conducting presentations and demonstrations related to Minor Projects, Major Projects, Skill-based projects, Internships, and other activities. The lab is equipped with advanced hardware facilities including an Antenna Testing facility, Spectrum Analyzer, Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO), PCB-prototyping machine, Function generator, PCB Soldering/De-soldering Station, etc. Ph.D. and M.Tech scholars also carry out their research in this lab.
   - Details / Manual: https://drive.google.com/file/d/13-B1ZaO457TekxwI8k5KsUagFGCnQUz5/view?usp=sharing

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

3. Computer Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate and Postgraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Basic Mathematical experiments using MATLAB / Scilab; Simulation of various engineering problems in MATLAB/Scilab and other tools; Qualnet: Network simulation using GNS; CST Studio: Antenna design and RF simulation.
   - Details / Manual: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/electronics_engineering/Computer%20Lab.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

4. Communication Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Sampling and reconstruction, pulse amplitude and pulse width modulation (PAM/PWM), generation and detection of Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK), Phase Shift Keying (PSK), and Frequency Shift Keying (FSK) signals using MATLAB / Scilab software and communication trainer kits.
   - Details / Manual: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KtvXGj_SZE8TRueuFaADbStcxCFuenRP/view?usp=sharing

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

5. Digital and Microprocessor Lab
   - Description: Undergraduate Lab. Major experiments are related to: Assembly language programming to generate standard waveforms using DAC and display waveforms on CRO with 8085; obtaining 2's complement of numbers; interfacing 8253 Timer and 8255 PPI with 8086 microprocessor in different operating modes.
   - Details / Manual: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kwYbtV1bugQ_w4Kfn5m4Kc61yaT4BNjL/view?usp=sharing

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Electronics Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Electronics Engineering

6. 5G Communication Network Lab (Developed by C-DOT)
   - Description: Developed by C-DOT (Centre for Development of Telematics), Bangalore at MITS-DU Gwalior, serving as an end-to-end 5G test bed solution. Benefits for students and faculty include:
     * Gaining practical insights into an end-to-end 5G system.
     * Developing a deeper understanding of 3GPP specifications for 5G RAN and Core networks.
     * Enhancing system capabilities while exploring new 5G use cases and applications.
     * Providing a foundation for advanced research and specification development for 6G technologies.
   - Details / Manual: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ij5i6IUNoUUbF7X7c6BcrpftcRFBkyQQ/view?usp=sharing
