Department: School of Humanities and Management
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

Department Vision:
To impart knowledge of subjects in Humanities that serves to complete the academic potential of a graduate student in the engineering stream.

Department Mission:
- To replace Communication Skills with Soft Skills - a paper with a more practical approach in improving communication and behavioural skills of students.
- To initiate papers in psychological and behavioural science so as to provide students the needed assistance in realising their goals.
- To initiate certificate and degree programmes so as to convert itself into a full-fledged department.
- To emphasise Entrepreneurship to enable students to generate employment instead of merely becoming employees.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Humanities And Management Department > About Humanities And Management Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Humanities And Management Department > About Humanities And Management Department]

About the Department:
The stream of Humanities has been an integral part of the Engineering Curricula since its inception, and the Department has delivered these courses with variations in syllabi and schemes according to the evolving needs of the times and student requirements. The Department at present has five faculty members and organizes additional and remedial classes for students in need.

Additional Classes Handled:
1. Special classes in Communication Skills and Personality Development.
2. English as a foundation course open to all students.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Humanities And Management Department > About Humanities And Management Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Humanities And Management Department > About Humanities And Management Department]

Extended Vision & Mission:
The Department engages classes for courses taught at both Undergraduate and Postgraduate levels. As it is imperative for every student to display proficiency in Language and Managerial Skills to be an effective executive, the aim of the Department is to inculcate the habit of speaking fluently, presenting views effectively, and developing strong leadership qualities. The Department seeks to achieve the all-round development of students by grooming their personality in both hard and soft skills. This enables students and faculty alike to pursue higher studies and advanced research for societal betterment and national advancement.

Section: About the Department

Department of Information Technology — MITS Gwalior
====================================================

Department Vision
-----------------

To produce competent IT professionals, promote technological innovation and connecting multidimensional aspects of IT for societal growth and development.

Department Mission
------------------

- To ensure high quality education based on practical approach and industrial demand.
- To facilitate emerging courses, training programs and workshops in the field of Information Technology and interdisciplinary areas.
- To promote research and development in the domain of Information Technology to meet the emerging needs of the Society.
- To promote technological innovation and entrepreneurship in the areas of IT with interdisciplinary connect.

About the Department
--------------------

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > About It Department

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > About It Department]
Section: About the Department

The Department of IT has an excellent & rich history and an outstanding record of contributions to the profession and community. The department is well recognized for excellence in facilities and teaching. The Department offers B.Tech. & M.Tech. programme in Information Technology and research program leading to PhD degree in Information Technology. 

The Department has a comprehensive curriculum on topics related to all aspects of Computer Hardware and Software with an emphasis on practical learning. The course structure is up-to-date and includes courses on emerging topics to equip our students with the latest developments in Information Technology.

Section: Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)

Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)
==========================================================

1. Data Science Lab
   - Description: Data Science Lab provides a computing platform for novel languages like Python and R for building a coherent set of ideas, fundamentals of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Deep Learning models and algorithms, and it facilitates students to practice basic programming in C, C++, and JAVA. Each lab session is aimed to translate theory lectures into practical implementation through programming paradigms, tools, and platforms provided in the data science lab.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)

2. Programming Lab
   - Description: Programming Lab welcomes students, researchers, interns, faculties, newbies, and everyone from a broad range of disciplines who are fascinated with the possibilities of turning big and complex data into knowledge. Members of the lab seek cutting-edge problem-based solutions to data mining, computer vision, and machine learning problems arising in numerous application areas involving data analytics.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)

3. Computing Lab
   - Description: The Computing Lab brings together researchers interested in developing fast, reliable, and robust numerical algorithms needed for modeling and simulation in a variety of fields including database management, numerical linear algebra, optimization, etc. The requirement of modern days is to have an automated system that manages, modifies, and updates data accurately. The lab aims at practicing and achieving this by using various software through hands-on training in programming and practical projects.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)

4. Project Lab
   - Description: Project Lab intends to deliver practical exposure towards mathematical background in linear algebra, analysis, probability, and optimization to develop the knowledge of machine learning to gain a deeper understanding of models and tools of great practical impact. It provides hands-on training in programming through practical projects. The goal is to enable students to independently apply the learned skills to real-world models and complex topics.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Information Technology Department > Laboratory]
Section: Laboratories — Department of Information Technology (IT)

5. Hardware and Microprocessor Lab
   - Description: The microprocessor is a multipurpose, programmable device that accepts digital data as input, processes it according to instructions stored in its memory, and provides results as output. The objective of the Microprocessor and Microcontroller Laboratory is to familiarize students with 8086 Microprocessor & 8051 Microcontroller assembly language programming and interfacing with various modules. It helps students to implement industrial and real-time applications by understanding core concepts of microprocessors and microcontrollers.

[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Internet Of Things Department > About Iot Department]

Department: Centre for Internet of Things (CIoT)
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

About the Centre for Internet of Things
The Centre for Internet of Things (CIoT) was established in 2023 with the vision of becoming a hub for innovation, research, and skill development in the rapidly evolving domain of Internet of Things.
The centre is offering two B.Tech. courses: "B.Tech in Internet of Things (IoT) and B.Tech in Electrical and Computer Engineering."
The centre aims to bridge the gap between academia and industry by providing hands-on training, interdisciplinary learning, and real-world problem-solving experiences.
The centre is equipped with advanced infrastructure, IoT development kits, sensors, microcontrollers, and cloud-enabled platforms to support innovative student projects, faculty research, industry collaborations, and real-world applications in smart agriculture, healthcare, smart cities, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
The centre serves as a platform to nurture entrepreneurial talent and develop IoT-enabled solutions that contribute to societal and industrial advancement.

[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Internet Of Things Department > About Iot Department]

Department Vision
To emerge as a center of excellence in the field of Internet of Things by driving innovation, interdisciplinary research, and skill development to empower technocrats who can lead digital transformation and deliver sustainable solutions for society.

Department Mission
- To provide quality education and practical exposure in IoT technologies through interdisciplinary and experiential learning.
- To cultivate innovation and entrepreneurship by developing IoT-based solutions for real-world challenges across various domains.
- To establish collaborations with industry, academia, and research institutions for advanced IoT research, training, and consultancy.
- To promote impactful research, publications, and skill-building programs that contribute to the global IoT ecosystem.

About B.Tech Programme in Mathematics and Computing:
B. Tech programme in Mathematics and Computing offers the opportunity to combine an appreciation of mathematical thinking with an knowledge of computing. Mathematics is a fundamental intellectual tool in computing, but computing is increasingly used as a key component in mathematical problem-solving. The course concentrates on areas where mathematics and computing are most relevant to each other, emphasizing the bridges between theory and practice. It offers opportunities for potential computer scientists to develop a deeper understanding of the mathematical foundations of their subject.

Department: Engineering Mathematics & Computing (Department of Mathematics & Computing)
Laboratories

1. Data Science Lab (DSL)
The Data Science Lab has been dedicated to provide a platform to students where theoretical lectures can be translated into practical implementation through programming models and tools. In Data Science Lab, our steady focus is to find the solutions of data-driven problems of Data Engineering, Data Analysis, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning so that data can be transformed into valuable insights. PYTHON is a highly productive scripting language that is used to provide high productivity and performance to process large amounts of data in data science. The students can practice other programming languages like C, C++, JAVA and MATLAB also. Once students understand how to use a language, they can write the source code in a text editor, execute it on an interpreter, or compile it for execution. Students try different approaches for invoking and executing PYTHON scripts and complete PYTHON coding exercises. In Data Science Lab, students perform experiments, gain experience and move forward.
View More Details: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/Departments/engineering_mathematics/Laboratories/view%20more%20detail_DSL%201.pdf

2. Computing Lab
The Computing Lab is very useful for the students, engineers, scientists & researchers. Millions of engineers and scientists worldwide use MATLAB for a range of applications in industry, including deep learning and machine learning, signal processing and communications, image and video processing, control systems, test and measurement, and computational finance. Students learn how to solve Numerical Analysis problems by using MATLAB. Numerical method is a mathematical tool designed to solve numerical problems. Numerical methods give us approximate results as there are always some assumptions made. The package MATLAB (matrix laboratory) provides an environment in which students can learn to program and explore the structure of numerical methods.

Department: Engineering Mathematics & Computing (Department of Mathematics & Computing)
Research Areas

The vision of the department is to impart knowledge of mathematics and computer sciences that serve to groom the academic potential of student and abreast with recent technological developments. With respect to potential areas of research of the Department in order to commercialize the research outcomes through development of products or services are:
1. Fluid Dynamics
2. Population Dynamics
3. Queuing theory
4. Statistical Techniques
5. Special functions

--- APPLICATIONS AND CURRENT RESEARCH WORK ---

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas]

1. Fluid Dynamics
The study of fluid dynamics yields different methods to understand weather predictions (weather forecasting), blood circulation, ocean currents, air conditioning systems, wind turbines, and rocket engines, etc. The current areas of research in fluid dynamics are Non-Newtonian Fluid Dynamics, Biological Fluid Dynamics, Microhydrodynamics, Hydrodynamic Instability and Transition to Turbulence, Geophysical and Environmental Fluid Dynamics (GEFD), Biological fluid Flows, and Nanofluid flow.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas]

2. Population Dynamics
The understanding of population dynamics enables us to know the relative importance of competition for resources and predation in ecological communities. It is an area of mathematics used to model and study the age and size composition of populations as dynamical systems. The current areas of research in population dynamics are management of natural resources, preserving biodiversity, cases of COVID-19, demography (Global Family Change (GFC)), Human resources and endowment, etc.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas]

3. Queuing Theory
Queuing theory is a branch of operational research (optimization engineering) that deals with the study of queues (waiting lines). The mathematical model of a queuing system enables us to predict waiting time and length of the queue. The application of queuing theory can be seen in scheduling (viz. jobs of machines, programs on computer, patients in hospital, etc.), traffic flow (aircraft, vehicles, telecommunication, etc.), and facility design (post offices, supermarkets, banks, etc.). The current research areas of queuing theory are in construction management, hospital pharmacy performance (controlling and monitoring medication), air defence missile weapon systems, etc.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas]

4. Statistical Techniques
Statistical techniques apply to descriptive statistics (dealing with properties of sample and population data) and inferential statistics (testing hypotheses and making conclusions). The current areas of research in statistical techniques are data mining and statistical analysis, data engineering, database management and architecture, business intelligence, and engineering and market data analysis.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mathematics And Computing Department > Research Areas]

5. Special Functions
Special functions lie in mathematical physics, which includes functions like gamma functions, beta functions, hypergeometric functions, Meijer G-function, Legendre's and Bessel's functions, Whittaker functions, Riemann zeta function and their extensions, etc. Current areas of special functions are in fractional calculus, astronomy, cardiac pacemaking function, analytic number theory, and coherent states, etc.

To enhance knowledge through project and internship in the field of Mechanical and allied engineering.
To guide students in acquiring career-oriented jobs in the field of Mechanical engineering.
To provide academic environment of excellence, leadership, ethical values and lifelong learning to cater the need of society by sustainable solutions.

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > About Mechanical Department]

Mechanical Engineering is an NBA-accredited program
Department of Mechanical Engineering is one of the oldest departments established in 1957 at MITS Gwalior. The Department offers academic programs at two levels leading to Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) and Master of Technology (M.Tech.). The department is dedicated to the teaching and research activities in the areas of production, design and thermal also in Automobile, Vibration, Energy and Renewable energy and Advanced Machining process. The department educates the students to take up challenging jobs in a wide range of industries and engage themselves in research and development activities for the good of society. The syllabi of the courses are continuously updated and the laboratories modernized to reflect the rapid changes in technology. It also offers high-quality research in the (ME and Ph.D.) programs. Department offers a variety of discipline electives and covers most of the modern technologies. It has state of the art laboratories to provide hands-on experiences and support research activities. A dynamic faculty and an experienced support staff give the department a breadth of academic focus and a wide range of technical expertise. Our full time experienced faculty members have a passion for teaching and an affirmed commitment to research and development.

[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Laboratories

Vibration Analysis Lab
The Reliability Training Centre consists of the latest equipment in bearing maintenance and condition monitoring fields which shall give a unique opportunity to students to attend hands-on training programs and practical sharing of knowledge.
Major Equipment: Mounting star (Bearing training kit), Bearing Mounting and Dismounting kit, Alignment rig with tools, Basic condition monitoring kit, Self-learning tool, FFT Analyser, Experimental test rigs, Online Learning tools.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

I C Engine Lab
Internal Combustion Engine Laboratory is a well-equipped laboratory that provides ideas on the practice of handling IC engines and measuring the performance parameters. This laboratory is scheduled for 4th-semester students of Automobile Engineering and 6th-semester students of the Mechanical engineering branch. The maximum tests which are performed on IC engines are for commercial purposes to find the following: The overload carrying capacity of the engine. The quantity of cooling water required on a brake power basis in kg per kW-hr. Brake Power (which is also known as rated power) with guaranteed fuel consumption.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Lab
The Refrigeration and Air-conditioning Lab consists of modern equipment in Vapour Compression Refrigeration System, Air-conditioning training system as well as various refrigeration test rigs which makes a unique platform for the students to perform their experimental practice in the refrigeration area.
Major Equipment: Vapour compression refrigeration trainer, Cold storage trainer, Air conditioning test rig, Duct able air conditioning test rig, cut section of various transmission, vapour compression refrigeration system, Direct and indirect type AC & Refrigeration and fault simulator

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Mechanics of Material Lab
Mechanical of Material Lab is currently engaging courses namely Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulic Machines (120314/190314) for Mechanical and Automobile branches respectively. This lab is run in conjunction with the theory course 120319/190317 (Mechanical of Material) under the first Department Core Subject. Mechanics of Materials is one of the important subjects in Mechanical as well as in Automotive Engineering. It is the physical science that looks at the reaction of a body to movement and deformation due to mechanical, thermal, and other loads.
Major Equipment: Universal Testing Machine, Rockwell Hardness Testing Machine, Extensometer, Fatigue Testing Machine, Pendulum Impact Tester, Surface Roughness Tester, Bending Moment Apparatus, Shear force Apparatus)

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Fluid Mechanics Lab
Fluid Mechanics & Fluid Machines Lab is currently engaging courses namely Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulic Machines (120314/190314) for Mechanical and Automobile branches respectively.
Major Equipments: Venturimeter Apparatus, Orificemeter Apparatus, Notch Apparatus, Metacentric Height Apparatus, Pipe Friction Apparatus, Bernoulli’s Apparatus, Centrifugal Pump Test Rig, Reciprocating Pump Test Rig, Pelton Turbine Test Rig, Francis Turbine Test Rig, Wind Tunnel (300x300 mm section)

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Heat & Mass Transfer Lab
Heat and Mass Transfer laboratory provides fundamental and industrial knowledge about modes of heat and mass transfer, like conduction, convection, radiation, mass transfer, and their application. The experimental setups in this laboratory are a part of the curriculum for third-year undergraduate students undertaking the course “Heat and Mass Transfer”. To enhance the practical knowledge of industrial equipment, students perform the practical on Shell-&-Tube heat exchanger, Parallel flow heat exchanger, finding Conductivity of metal rod and insulating powder, experiments to determine convective heat transfer coefficient in various materials, the performance of pin fin of various materials apparatus and experiment to understand Kirchhoff’s and Stefan Boltzman laws.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Dynamics of Machine Lab
Dynamics of Machine Lab is currently engaging courses namely Theory of Machine-I & Theory of Machine-II for Mechanical and Automobile branches respectively.
The following apparatus is there in the Dynamics of Machine Lab: Governors Apparatus, Gyroscopic Apparatus, Moment of inertia Apparatus, Dynamometer Apparatus, Clutch Apparatus, Brakes Apparatus, Four bar mechanism, and slider crank mechanism.

CAD/CAM Lab
CAD/CAM Lab is engaging courses namely Design of Machine Elements (120402), Machine design (120515), and Software lab 120315/190315 for Mechanical and Automobile Engineering students. Following software and machines are there in COMPUTER-AIDED DESIGN AND COMPUTER-AIDED MANUFACTURING LAB.
Software: AutoCAD, CATIA, ANSYS
Major Equipment: 3D Printer, CNC Lathe, CNC Milling Machine, Robotic Arm, 25 Computers

metadata.breadcrumbs: Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Academic > School & Centre > Mechanical Department > Laboratory]

Basic Mechanical Engineering Lab
Mechanical Engineering is often considered the most basic type of engineering work. It is probably the first branch of engineering which has vast applications in all fields. Mechanical engineers were responsible for Industrial Revolution and innovations like the steam engine, internal combustion engines, turbines, compressors, pneumatic machines, machine tools, refrigeration, air conditioning systems, etc done by mechanical engineers. Therefore every student should know the basics of mechanical engineering.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Admission > Faqs

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Admission > Faqs]
Section: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (ADMISSIONS)

Q1: What is the admission process for B.Tech at MITS Gwalior?
A: B.Tech admissions at MITS are conducted primarily through JEE Main scores and Madhya Pradesh state online counselling conducted by Directorate of Technical Education (DTE MP). Key steps include:
   1. Appear in the JEE Main examination.
   2. Register for MP DTE online counselling at https://dte.mponline.gov.in.
   3. Fill branch and institute choices (select MITS Gwalior and preferred branches).
   4. Attend document verification and receive seat allotment.
   5. Report to MITS, submit required documents, and pay the admission fee.

Q2: What is the admission process for B.Arch?
A: Admissions to Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) are based on NATA scores and/or JEE Main Paper 2 scores through DTE MP online counselling.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Admission > Faqs

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Admission > Faqs]
Section: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (ADMISSIONS)

Q3: What are the admission criteria for PG programs (M.Tech, MCA, MBA)?
A:
- M.Tech / M.E.: Based on GATE scores and qualifying degree marks through DTE MP counselling.
- MCA: Based on MP Pre-MCA test or qualifying graduation merit through DTE MP.
- MBA: Based on CMAT / qualifying graduation scores through DTE MP counselling.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Admission > Faqs

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Admission > Faqs]
Section: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (ADMISSIONS)

Q4: What documents are required at the time of admission?
A: Candidates must bring original and photocopies of:
   - 10th and 12th Marksheets & Passing Certificates
   - Entrance Exam Score Card (JEE Main / GATE / NATA / CMAT / Pre-MCA)
   - MP DTE Seat Allotment Letter
   - Transfer Certificate (TC) & Migration Certificate
   - Character Certificate
   - Caste Certificate, Income Certificate & Domicile Certificate (if applicable)
   - Aadhaar Card & Passport size photographs
   - Medical fitness certificate
   Detailed list: https://web.mitsgwalior.in/images/2026/july/Admission%20documents_compressed.pdf

metadata.breadcrumbs: Admission > Faqs

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Admission > Faqs]
Section: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (ADMISSIONS)

Q5: What scholarships are available for students at MITS?
A:
- SC/ST/OBC Post-Matric Scholarships via the MPTAASC portal.
- Mukhyamantri Medhavi Vidyarthi Yojana (MMVY) by the Government of MP (refer to https://scholarship.mitsgwalior.in).
- Gaon Ki Beti Yojana for eligible female students from rural areas.
- Pragati & Saksham Scholarships by AICTE.
- Merit scholarships and tuition fee waivers under the TFW (Tuition Fee Waiver) Scheme.

Q6: Is hostel accommodation available for first-year students?
A: Yes, hostel facilities are available for both boys and girls with 24x7 security, mess, Wi-Fi, recreation hall, and sports facilities. Hostel registration can be done via Google Form: https://forms.gle/b7Wm3Zjv8i2KDUHv7.

================================================================================
INSTITUTIONAL DESCRIPTION:
================================================================================
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior, India was established in 1957 by His Highness Sir Jiwaji Rao Scindia, Maharaja of the erstwhile state of Gwalior under the open door policy of the Government of India.
- Foundation Stone: Laid by the then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, on 20th October, 1956.
- Inauguration: Inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan on 11th December, 1964.
- Golden Jubilee: Graced by the President of India, Dr. Pratibha Devisingh Patil, as Chief Guest on 30th June, 2008, where a commemorative Indian postal stamp on MITS was officially released.

================================================================================
INSTITUTIONAL DESCRIPTION:
================================================================================
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior, India was established in 1957 by His Highness Sir Jiwaji Rao Scindia, Maharaja of the erstwhile state of Gwalior under the open door policy of the Government of India.
- Foundation Stone: Laid by the then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, on 20th October, 1956.
- Inauguration: Inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan on 11th December, 1964.
- Golden Jubilee: Graced by the President of India, Dr. Pratibha Devisingh Patil, as Chief Guest on 30th June, 2008, where a commemorative Indian postal stamp on MITS was officially released.

OVERVIEW:
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Deemed University, Gwalior, has successfully organized seven editions of the flagship International Conference on Sustainable and Innovative Solutions for Current Challenges in Engineering & Technology (ICSISCET - 2019 to 2025), four editions of the International Student Conference on Multidisciplinary and Current Technical Research (ISCMCTR - 2023 to 2026), and the IEEE International Conference on Electrical, Communication, and Computing Technologies (iCONECCT-2025). These international forums bring together global researchers, academicians, and industry experts to disseminate cutting-edge research in computational sciences, sustainable technology, and engineering innovation.

SIMILARITY THRESHOLDS & VERIFICATION:
- All research scholars, PG students, and faculty members must submit an official similarity report generated via Turnitin / Urkund (Ouriginal) along with their dissertation/thesis submission.

- Manuscripts exceeding permissible thresholds are returned to the candidate for revision and re-evaluation.

R&D — Testing & Consultancy
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior
(Deemed to be University)

OVERVIEW:
MITS Gwalior is a recognized hub for industrial testing, calibration, design vetting, and technical consultancy services across Madhya Pradesh and Central India. The institute leverages its state-of-the-art laboratories and domain-expert faculty to deliver specialized consultancy for government bodies, public sector undertakings, and private enterprises.

metadata.breadcrumbs: R & D > Testing And Consultancy

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | R & D > Testing And Consultancy]

MAJOR CONSULTANCY DOMAINS & SERVICES:
1. Civil & Structural Engineering:
   - Soil investigation & geotechnical testing.
   - Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) of concrete structures, bridges, and buildings.
   - Material testing: cement, steel, coarse/fine aggregates, bitumen, and bricks.
   - Structural design verification and vetting for public infrastructure projects.
   - Third-party quality inspection and monitoring for government municipal corporations, PWD, NHAI, and smart city projects.

2. Electrical & Electronics Engineering:
   - Energy auditing and electrical power quality analysis.
   - High-voltage testing and calibration of electrical instruments.
   - Embedded systems and IoT prototyping for industrial automation.

metadata.breadcrumbs: R & D > Testing And Consultancy

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | R & D > Testing And Consultancy]

3. Mechanical Engineering:
   - Vibration analysis, acoustic measurement, and dynamic balancing.
   - Thermal efficiency analysis of boilers and heat exchangers.
   - Material characterization, tensile testing, and hardness evaluation.

4. Environmental & Chemical Engineering:
   - Water and wastewater quality analysis (BOD, COD, heavy metals).
   - Air pollution monitoring and environmental impact assessments.

5. Computer Science & Information Technology:
   - Enterprise software design, security auditing, and cloud infrastructure setup.
   - AI-driven analytics, automation, and computer vision solutions.

Student Life — Facilities
Learning Resource Centre (Central Library)
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

Overview:
Welcome to the Central Library, Madhav Institute of Technology & Science — a very special place on the MITS campus with its rich collection of books and journals in the field of Engineering and Architecture related disciplines. The Central Library currently houses around 1,00,000 books, comprising textbooks and reference books for Engineering Graduates (UG), Postgraduates (PG), and Ph.D. curriculum in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics, Electrical, Computer Science & Information Technology, and Architecture disciplines. The library collection also includes documents in Computer Science, History of Science, Fiction, Stories, General books, Encyclopaedias, Dictionaries, and Magazines.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre]

Digital Library & RFID Automation:
The Central Library recently automated its library services; in the Gwalior region, MITS Central Library is the first to implement RFID technology with international security standards (ISO-15693 / ISO 18000-3), operating on 13.56 MHz. In the last 12 months, more than 38,651 books were issued to various UG/PG students. It is an effective automated system used worldwide for managing library collections and providing enhanced services to users, offering benefits such as:
- Theft control and misplaced reading material tracking
- Sorting, inventory accuracy, and stock verification procedures
- Security control, video surveillance, and Smart Card integration
All books are tagged with the latest RFID technology. For issuing books, students present their Smart Card at the circulation counter. Upon transaction completion, students receive issue/return status via SMS on their mobile or can check transaction status on their individual dashboard under the "My Books Issued Status" tab.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre]

Archive Section:
The Library maintains an archive section of rare and vintage books dating back to 1950. This valuable collection caters to the needs of research scholars. The library also houses a rich collection of over 1,000 M.Tech Dissertations and Ph.D. theses.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre]

Key Services:
- Circulation: Weekly branch-wise issue and return facility so all students can avail the collection.
- Open Access System: Facilitates students to search and browse required material directly on the shelves.
- Reprographic Services: Photocopy services provided on demand.
- Computer Lab: Dedicated computer lab with 15 computers inside the library for accessing E-books, E-journals, and online resources. High-speed Wi-Fi is available in and around the library.
- E-Journals: Subscribes to international e-journal databases covering 620+ titles across engineering disciplines: (a) IEEE (b) ASME (c) ASCE (d) ScienceDirect. Central Library also subscribes to print national and international journals. E-journals are accessible 24/7 across the campus via a dedicated leased line.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre]

Library Timings:
- Working Hours: 10:00 AM to 8:30 PM on all working days.

Integrated Library Management System (ILMS):
- Software: Koha (Version: 3.18)
- Nature of Automation: Fully Automated (Automated in 2014 with RFID & Institute ERP integration; Koha adopted in 2016)
- Features: Web-based ILS with MariaDB/MySQL back end, MARC cataloguing, Z39.50/SRU support, Web 2.0 (tagging, RSS, comments), union catalogue, online circulation, barcode/RFID, and member card printing.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Learning Resource Centre]

Library Rules & Loan Privileges:
- General category students: 5 books for 4 weeks (renewable for another 4 weeks if not reserved).
- SC/ST category students: 7 books for 4 weeks (renewable for another 4 weeks if not reserved).
- Overdue Fine: Rs. 1/- per day per book (excludes 2nd & 3rd Saturdays, Sundays, and state government holidays). If fine exceeds book value, rules for loss of books apply.

Lost Book Recovery Rules:
1. Replace with the latest edition of the material plus an additional charge of Rs. 100/- towards RFID tag and administrative costs; OR
2. Pay the cost of the latest edition plus Rs. 100/- towards RFID tag and administrative costs; OR
3. If out of print or rare, pay twice (2x) the cost of the book plus Rs. 100/- towards RFID tag and administrative costs.

Student Life — Facilities
Central Workshop
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

Overview:
The workshop is the heart of the engineering curriculum in general, and practically for the Mechanical Engineering discipline. Here, students are exposed to various manufacturing processes with critical study of process parameters. Central Workshop, a core unit of Madhav Institute of Technology & Science, Gwalior, was established in 1957. The workshop possesses spacious working areas, sophisticated machinery, and tools for performing diverse practical experiments.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Workshop

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Workshop]

Academic Role:
Basic training in the workshop satisfies degree requirements for all engineering branches during their first or second semester. In addition, practical classes for B.E./B.Tech (Mechanical Engineering) and M.Tech (Production Engineering) are conducted with the guidance of experienced faculty and technical staff in various specialized shops.

Equipment & Upgrades:
- Advanced Machines: Electro Discharge Machining (EDM), Electro Chemical Machining (ECM), and Plasma Cutting machines are installed alongside conventional machine tools.
- Modern Upgradation: Installation of NC and CNC machines with ongoing renovation to meet contemporary industry 4.0 standards.
- Industrial Interaction: Supports industrial product development and fosters strong industry-institute interaction.

metadata.breadcrumbs: Student Life > Facilities > Workshop

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | Student Life > Facilities > Workshop]

Institute Maintenance Services:
The Central Workshop undertakes regular maintenance activities across the campus:
- Electrical, welding, and carpentry repairs for the institute, student hostels, staff quarters, faculty cabins, and departmental laboratories.
- Manages electric and water supply distribution, including diesel generator backup power systems and inventory control for campus infrastructure maintenance.

Specialized Shops in Central Workshop:
1. Machine Shop
2. Foundry Shop
3. Fitting Shop
4. Welding Shop
5. Carpentry Shop
6. Smithy Shop
7. Production Lab

================================================================================
Who We Are:
A community of passionate developers, innovators, and tech enthusiasts building the future together at MITS Gwalior.

Our Mission:
To empower students with practical software development skills, foster innovation through collaborative projects, and bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements. We believe in learning by doing and growing together as a community.

To become the leading platform for student developers to learn, collaborate, and innovate. We envision a future where every student has the skills and confidence to build amazing software that solves real-world problems and makes a positive impact.

- Workshops: Regular coding workshops and tech talks on the latest technologies.
- Hackathons: Organize and participate in competitive coding events and campus hackathons.
- Mentorship: Peer-to-peer learning and guidance from experienced members and alumni.
- Open Source: Contribute to open source projects and build strong developer portfolios.
- Campus Portals: Build and maintain core digital infrastructure, automation tools, and portals for MITS Gwalior.

Student Life — Students Grievances & Counselling
Girls Grievance & Gender Sensitization Cell
Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior

Overview:
In order to create an environment of gender equity in the institute and to specifically address all types of grievances of the female students of the institute, the Girls Grievance Cell has been constituted. The members of the cell constantly interact among themselves and with the girls on the campus to look into any particular issues or problems faced by the girls and strive to take necessary action at the earliest. The idea is to create an atmosphere which is conducive to the all-round development of the female students and to provide them with a platform where they can fearlessly share their issues.

- To equip the female students with the knowledge of their special legal rights.

- To deal with cases and complaints of any type of harassment of the female students of the Institute.
- To provide assistance and support in creating a congenial and secure atmosphere for girls.
- To create opportunities for all-round personality development of female students.

The Goal of the Training & Placement Cell of MITS Gwalior is to act as a vital liaison between industry and students to provide employment opportunities available in the market and to provide intensive training to students for their overall career development.
It works under the guidance of the Training & Placement Officer in consultation with the Faculty In-Charge and student placement coordinators.

## 2. Historical Milestones & Heritage

- Founded: 1957 by His Highness Sir Jiwaji Rao Scindia, Maharaja of the erstwhile State of Gwalior, under the open-door policy of the Government of India.
- Foundation Stone: Laid by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, on 28th October 1956.
- Building Inauguration: Inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan on 11th December 1964.
- Golden Jubilee: Graced by the President of India, Dr. Pratibha Devi Singh Patil, as Chief Guest on 30th June 2008. A commemorative postal stamp on MITS was released by India Post.
- Deemed University Milestone: Granted Deemed-to-be-University status under Distinct Category by the Ministry of Education, Govt. of India, on UGC advice in March 2024.

metadata.breadcrumbs: 03 Academics Courses And Curriculum

content:

Section: 4. Key Academic Features & NEP-2020 Implementation

- Multiple Entry & Multiple Exit (MEME): Direct admissions to 2nd and 3rd year UG programs under MEME guidelines.
- Relative Statistical Grading: Implemented across all B.Tech and MCA courses to eliminate exam paper difficulty bias.
- Mandatory Digital Skills: Python, Data Science, and Machine Learning are compulsory foundational courses for all students regardless of engineering branch.
- Minor Degree Specializations: Students from conventional branches can earn Minor Degrees in AI, IoT, Robotics, Data Science, or Cyber Security.
- Novel Engaging Courses (NEC): Compulsory courses in II Semester focused on hands-on practical skills and multidisciplinary development.
- Continuous Evaluation: Weekly LMS quizzes, mid-term evaluations, project exhibitions, and laboratory proficiencies.

metadata.breadcrumbs: 04 Academic Calendars And Regulations

content:
[MITS Knowledge Base | 04 Academic Calendars And Regulations]
Section: 4. Academic Regulations & Guidelines

1. Attendance Mandate: Students must maintain minimum mandatory attendance as per MITS-DU ordinances tracked on the Academic Management System (AMS). Shortage leads to debarment.
2. Compulsory Continuous Assessment: Submitting weekly quizzes, lab assignments, and project deliverables is strictly mandatory.
3. Make-Up Evaluation Policy: Make-up evaluation is strictly permitted only for valid/bonafide documented reasons with advance approval from Class Coordinators and Head of Department. Full syllabus is tested.
4. Relative Grading: Statistical relative grading is applied to all undergraduate courses (ME/M.Tech use standard grading).
5. Summer Semester: An optional fast-track semester conducted at the end of each academic year to allow students to clear backlogs and improve CGPA if below the minimum 5.0 CGPA threshold.
6. Pre-Result Review: Students can formally challenge and apply for pre-result review of major evaluation papers before final grade finalization.

- Qualifying Exam: 10+2 examination from Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education (MPBSE) or equivalent recognized Central/State Board (CBSE, ICSE, etc.).

metadata.breadcrumbs: Mits Master Knowledge Base

Section: Vision

- Founded: 1957 by His Highness Sir Jiwaji Rao Scindia, Maharaja of the erstwhile State of Gwalior, under the open-door policy of the Government of India.
- Foundation Stone: Laid by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, on 28th October 1956.
- Building Inauguration: Inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan on 11th December 1964.
- Golden Jubilee: Graced by the President of India, Dr. Pratibha Devi Singh Patil, as Chief Guest on 30th June 2008. A commemorative postal stamp on MITS was released by India Post.
- Deemed University Milestone: Granted Deemed-to-be-University status under Distinct Category by the Ministry of Education, Govt. of India, on UGC advice in March 2024.

  * Hands-on innovation: State-of-the-art laboratories in Robotics, Machine Learning, AR/VR, IoT, and Drone Technology.
  * Research & Doctoral expansion: Expanding funded Ph.D. programs and high-productivity research in national thrust areas.

Section: 4. Academic Regulations & Guidelines

1. Attendance Mandate: Students must maintain minimum mandatory attendance as per MITS-DU ordinances tracked on the Academic Management System (AMS). Shortage leads to debarment.
2. Compulsory Continuous Assessment: Submitting weekly quizzes, lab assignments, and project deliverables is strictly mandatory.
3. Make-Up Evaluation Policy: Make-up evaluation is strictly permitted only for valid/bonafide documented reasons with advance approval from Class Coordinators and Head of Department. Full syllabus is tested.
4. Relative Grading: Statistical relative grading is applied to all undergraduate courses (ME/M.Tech use standard grading).
5. Summer Semester: An optional fast-track semester conducted at the end of each academic year to allow students to clear backlogs and improve CGPA if below the minimum 5.0 CGPA threshold.
6. Pre-Result Review: Students can formally challenge and apply for pre-result review of major evaluation papers before final grade finalization.
